content.value_statement: Teams often miss quality gaps when testing work is split across tools. This skill organizes unit, integration, E2E, browser, performance, and review workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides testing strategy across unit, integration, E2E, browser, performance, and review phases.
Provides copy-ready prompts for invoking specialized testing, QA, code review, and linting skills.
Lists concrete actions for fixtures, mocks, test data, screenshots, benchmarks, and CI integration.
Defines a quality gate checklist covering coverage, passing tests, E2E paths, benchmarks, scans, reviews, and linting.
Organizes related workflow bundles for development, security audit, cloud DevOps, and AI testing contexts.
limitations: It does not include executable test scripts or framework configuration files.
It depends on separate named skills that may not be installed or trusted.
It does not validate project-specific coverage or runtime results by itself.
Browser and screenshot steps require user-approved tools and safe test environments.

use_cases.title: Set Up a Test Plan
use_cases.description: Create a phased testing plan before a new project or major feature starts.

use_cases.title: Build Web App QA Coverage
use_cases.description: Coordinate unit, integration, E2E, browser, visual, and responsive testing for a web application.

use_cases.title: Prepare Release Quality Gates
use_cases.description: Define release checks for coverage, performance, security scans, code review, and linting.

prompt_templates.title: Create a QA Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-qa workflow to create a checklist for a small web app release. Include unit, integration, E2E, and lint checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a small release

prompt_templates.title: Plan Test Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-qa workflow to plan test coverage for a new API feature. Include fixtures, mocks, integration paths, and CI gates.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Browser QA
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-qa workflow to coordinate browser automation, visual checks, screenshots, and responsive testing for a checkout flow.

prompt_templates.title: Design Release Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the testing-qa workflow to design release quality gates for a production service. Include coverage, E2E, performance, security, and review criteria.

output_examples.input: Plan QA for a new user registration feature.
output: Recommended phases: strategy, unit tests, integration tests, E2E tests, browser checks, and release gates.
Key checks: validation rules, API errors, account creation flow, responsive screens, and coverage threshold.
Gate result: release is ready only after tests pass, review is complete, and linting is clean.

output_examples.input: Prepare browser testing for a marketing site launch.
output: Recommended browser tasks: headless checks, screenshot review, visual regression, and responsive layout verification.
Safety note: capture only approved test pages and avoid pages with private customer data.
Gate result: publish after screenshots are reviewed and critical paths pass on supported viewports.

output_examples.input: Create release quality gates for an API service.
output: Recommended gates: unit coverage, integration paths, mocked external services, performance benchmark, security scan, and code review.
Required evidence: passing test report, benchmark summary, review approval, and clean lint result.
Gate result: block release when a critical path, security scan, or benchmark fails.

best_practices: Confirm each referenced helper skill is installed and trusted before use.
Run tests in isolated environments with test data, not production accounts.
Tie every quality gate to a measurable result or reviewer decision.
anti_patterns: Using this workflow as a substitute for project-specific test design.
Capturing browser screenshots on pages with secrets or customer data.
Approving releases from generated plans without running the actual tests.

faq.question: Does this skill write test code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates testing phases and prompts. Separate testing skills or manual work create the actual tests.

faq.question: Can it support both frontend and backend testing?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers unit, integration, API, E2E, browser, performance, and release quality checks.

faq.question: Does it require other skills to work well?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow references specialized helper skills, so availability depends on the user environment.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with production data?
faq.answer: Use test data where possible. Browser screenshots and automation should avoid secrets and customer information.

faq.question: Can it define release gates?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checks for coverage, passing tests, E2E paths, benchmarks, scans, review, and linting.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
